subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Analysis of language, form and structure

questions.q: Who wrote the novella 'A Christmas Carol'?
questions.explain: Charles Dickens published 'A Christmas Carol' in 1843.

questions.q: In which Shakespeare play do three witches greet the protagonist with prophecies?
questions.explain: The three witches deliver their prophecies to Macbeth in Act 1.

questions.q: Who is the author of 'Frankenstein'?
questions.explain: Mary Shelley wrote 'Frankenstein', first published in 1818.

questions.q: The character Shylock appears in which Shakespeare play?
questions.explain: Shylock is the Jewish moneylender in 'The Merchant of Venice'.

questions.q: 'The Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde' was written by whom?
questions.explain: Robert Louis Stevenson published the novella in 1886.

questions.q: 'The Sign of Four' centres on which detective?
questions.explain: 'The Sign of Four' is an Arthur Conan Doyle Sherlock Holmes novel.

questions.q: In 'Romeo and Juliet', the two feuding families are the Montagues and the who?
questions.explain: Juliet belongs to the Capulet family and Romeo to the Montagues.

questions.q: In 'A Christmas Carol', what is the name of Scrooge's dead business partner whose ghost visits him?
questions.explain: Marley's ghost warns Scrooge and announces the three spirits.

questions.q: In 'The Tempest', Prospero's ability to raise the storm through magic chiefly establishes him as a figure of what over the island?
questions.explain: Prospero's magic marks him as the controlling authority on the island.

questions.q: When the audience of 'Romeo and Juliet' knows Juliet is only sleeping while Romeo believes she is dead, Shakespeare creates which effect?
questions.explain: Dramatic irony arises when the audience knows more than the character.

questions.q: 'A Christmas Carol' is widely read as an allegory criticising the treatment of the poor in which period?
questions.explain: Dickens attacks Victorian attitudes to poverty, including the workhouse system.

questions.q: 'Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde' is most often interpreted as exploring which central idea?
questions.explain: The novella dramatises the good and evil sides within a single person.

questions.q: In 'Macbeth', Lady Macbeth's obsessive hand-washing and cry of 'Out, damned spot!' dramatise her overwhelming sense of what?
questions.explain: Her sleepwalking exposes the guilt she cannot wash away.

questions.q: In 'Pride and Prejudice', Elizabeth Bennet's early mistaken judgement of Mr Darcy chiefly illustrates which theme?
questions.explain: Elizabeth's premature judgement embodies the 'prejudice' of the title.

questions.q: In 'Frankenstein', the creature turns to violence largely because he experiences what?
questions.explain: The creature becomes vengeful after being abandoned and shunned by all.

questions.q: Scrooge's transformation from miser to generous benefactor makes 'A Christmas Carol' centrally a story of what?
questions.explain: The narrative structure charts Scrooge's moral redemption across the staves.

questions.q: A student argues that blood imagery shows guilt Macbeth cannot remove. Which quotation best supports this point?
options: Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood clean from my hand?
Is this a dagger which I see before me?
Fair is foul, and foul is fair
questions.explain: Macbeth's image of unwashable blood directly conveys inescapable guilt.

questions.q: Analysing 'Is this a dagger which I see before me', which reading is best supported by the play?
options: Macbeth hallucinates the dagger as ambition drives him towards murder
Macbeth describes a real weapon handed to him by Banquo
The dagger is a gift given to Macbeth by King Duncan
Lady Macbeth is speaking these lines to Macbeth
questions.explain: The 'dagger of the mind' is a hallucination reflecting his murderous intent.

questions.q: A student analyses Marley's line 'I wear the chain I forged in life'. The strongest point is that the chain symbolises what?
options: The lasting consequences of a selfish, greedy life
questions.explain: The chain Marley forged represents the moral burden of his miserly life.

questions.q: For an essay on setting reflecting character in 'Jekyll and Hyde', which detail best supports the argument?
options: Hyde's shabby, sinister door contrasting with the respectable Jekyll house front
The sunny gardens where children happily play
The busy shipping docks of London
questions.explain: The neglected door mirrors Hyde's degraded nature against Jekyll's respectability.

specSource: AQA GCSE English Literature (8702) specification; Paper 1: Shakespeare and the 19th-century Novel
